title: How a harness makes a weak model finish the job
subtitle: Plain code around the model (tools, guardrails, context, verify) that ties a black-box agent to something stable.
hook: Same prompt, same weak model: harness code alone turned a failing agent into a working one.

sources.title: Harnesses in AI: A Deep Dive
sources.speaker: Tejas Kumar

nodes.label: Run harness
nodes.detail: The entry point. It runs the whole agent as one attempt and retries, giving up after three attempts.
nodes.tradeoff: A harness can be a loop around your agent loop; here it enforces max attempts at the harness level.

nodes.label: Context builder
nodes.detail: Starts with a basic system prompt and the user's task. When messages pile up, it keeps those two plus the last two messages.
nodes.tradeoff: The speaker calls this compressor super naive and says better ways exist.

nodes.label: Agent loop
nodes.detail: A while-true loop: get the model's next step, run it, push the events to a trace, stop when the model says it is done.
nodes.tradeoff: A harness is not just the agent loop; it is the stuff around the agent loop.

nodes.label: Model
nodes.detail: GPT-3.5 Turbo, a 2023 model picked on purpose to show a harness can make a weak model do the job.
nodes.tradeoff: Rented models are black boxes; a provider could serve a different model and you would never know.

nodes.label: Tool registry
nodes.detail: Each tool has a name, description, parameters and an execute function. Here they drive a Chromium browser through plain Playwright.
nodes.tradeoff: Plain Playwright, not Playwright MCP: tools are just traditional engineering.

nodes.label: Guardrails
nodes.detail: Max iterations kills the run after six steps. Max messages triggers context compression.
nodes.tradeoff: They are small functions that compose, so you can stack as many as you want.

nodes.label: Login handler
nodes.detail: Runs every loop step. On a login page it fills credentials, submits, and tells the agent the harness logged in.
nodes.tradeoff: Almost free when not on a login page, and secrets stay in harness code, not the model.

nodes.label: Trace history
nodes.detail: Every agent event is pushed into one history list. The harness reads it later instead of trusting the model's word.
nodes.tradeoff: The logs showed the first agent clicked upvote, hit a login screen, and still called it a success.

nodes.label: Verify step
nodes.detail: Plain code checks the trace: did the upvote click really succeed, and did any login step fail or go unhandled?
nodes.tradeoff: In a coding agent, the same step runs lint and tests to make sure nothing broke.

flow.text: Starts attempt one of at most three for the upvote task.
Packs a basic system prompt and the task into messages.
Loops until the model says it is done, capped at six steps.
GPT-3.5 Turbo picks the next action, like clicking upvote.
Playwright clicks upvote and Hacker News redirects to a login page.
The harness spots the login page, signs in, and tells the agent.
Each step's events are pushed into the trace history.
Code checks the trace for a real upvote before reporting success.

takeaways.text: A harness is everything around the model that grounds it in reality. The goal is reliability.
The prompt never changed. Harness code alone turned a failing GPT-3.5 Turbo agent into one that worked.
With a great harness, cheap or free models can go very far.
